Diane — appreciate the detail. We can do a staged-uplift path that preserves your base commit pricing and offers an "opt-in co-term" for incremental capacity. High-level proposal below; attaching a workbook with unit math.

Summary proposal (short):
- Base commit: keep existing annual commit and pricing intact (no retro increase).
- Staged uplifts: allow up to 3 mid-contract top-ups during the 12-month term. Each top-up gets a protected, stepped rate tier for the remainder of the term.
- Usage protection: a 90-day usage-averaging safeguard so one-off spikes don't lock you into the next tier.
- Proration: monthly proration on added units; if you add less than 30% of base in a month, we apply a micro-proration with no tier escalation unless sustained for 60 days.
- Co-term opt-in: you can elect to co-term the added capacity to next renewal at a pre-negotiated discount band (examples in workbook).

Next steps I propose: 1) Marcus will share a pricing worksheet with exact $/token bands; 2) you route to procurement for their must-haves; 3) we draft a short SOW amendment + billing exhibit to add to the renewal.

Attaching: redwood_staged_uplift_workbook.xlsx (pricing examples) and a draft SOW template.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the model.

Thanks,

Diane — quick follow with the concrete numbers referenced in Jordan's workbook. Key lines:

- Current base: 1M inference units/mo at $0.0022/unit (annual commit).
- Staged top-up tiers (examples):
  * Tier A (up to +25%): $0.0020/unit for added units (protected for remainder of term)
  * Tier B (+25% to +50%): $0.00185/unit on the incremental amount above 25%
  * Burst (episodic >50%): billed at on-demand rate but not escalatory unless sustained >90 days average

Example: if you add +40% in June, the first +25% is charged at Tier A, next +15% at Tier B (both protected through term) assuming you opt-in. Workbook has a month-by-month cashflow.

Notes on discounts: we can offer an additional 3% volume rebate on cumulative uplift if total annualized consumption exceeds 1.5x base by the end of the term. This is a limited incentive and can be scoped into the billing exhibit.

I can join a call if procurement wants the worksheet walked through line by line.

-Marcus

Thanks — noted. Attached is a suggested billing exhibit draft and a sample invoice layout (see attached acme_co-term_sow_draft.pdf for the exhibit section and redwood_staged_uplift_workbook.xlsx for the invoice examples). Quick answers inline: 

1) 90-day averaging exhibit: we propose language that defines a 90-day rolling average measured at month-end; if the rolling average of added units exceeds the top-up threshold for 90 consecutive days the top-up tier becomes permanent for the remainder of the term unless Acme elects to rollback in writing within 30 days. (Exact wording in the attached exhibit.)
2) Confirmed: no retroactive price changes for already billed periods; protections only apply prospectively from the invoice that includes the added units.
3) Sample invoice: line items will include "Base monthly commit" (unit count & unit price), "Staged top-up — month X" (added units, tier, per-unit price), and "Applied rebate accrual" (if any). Format attached in workbook as CSV example.
4) Rebate settlement: default is a true-up credit on the final invoice of the term; if you prefer monthly accruals we can apply pro-rated credits monthly — pick the preferred path and we'll update the exhibit.
